reason: Lobes, teeth, leaf apices and fruits that are 'sharply tipped' end in a sharp point. That is PATO:0002258 pointed, which is also the parent of FLOPO spine-tipped and acute (sensu botany).
This compares the part with another part (the tube): equality, with the tube as the second term. It is not a unary quality.
Well-marked veins, ridges, auricles and shields (French 'bien marquées') are clearly visible. This is the same reading as the earlier rules for 'distinct' and 'evident' (PATO:0000463).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: awn (PO_0025349) + increased length (PATO_0000573))
reason: The word says that an awn is present and that the awn is long. It is the quality of a part of the bearer, not a quality of the glume or lemma itself.

label: shrub-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a whole plant by virtue of its having several woody stems that arise from or near the ground and no single main trunk, as in a shrub. NOTE: Habit analogy, sibling of FLOPO:0991039 palm-like; not a statement that the plant is a shrub.
reason: This is a habit quality used across 5 floras (French 'arbustive'), and neither PATO nor FLOPO has it. The previous review set the precedent with palm-like.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (part of the bearer: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) + prominent (PATO_0001482))
reason: The quality belongs to the veins of the leaf, which stand out from the surface (French 'nervures saillantes'). 'Not prominently veined' is the negation of the same statement.

label: semi-obovate
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being one lengthwise half of an obovate figure, broadest above the middle and with one side straight or nearly so. NOTE: Built like PATO:0002232 semicircular; usual on legume pods, keel petals and wings.
reason: This is a standard botanical shape for asymmetric legume pods and petals. It cannot be expressed as obovate (PATO:0001936) plus 'asymmetrical' without losing which half is meant.
A shape between linear and obovate, made of two values. Most examples are really linear-oblanceolate (PATO:0002330), which is handled the same way.
This negates rigid, which earlier rule C186 mapped to PATO:0001545 inflexible. 'Firm but not rigid' does not claim 'flexible', so the negation is safer than PATO:0001544.

label: basipetal
definition: A structural quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its flowers developing or opening in succession from the apex towards the base. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991034 indeterminate; 'dehiscence basipetal' of fruits (opening from apex to base) is a different sense and is not covered.
reason: The order of flowering is a real inflorescence character that has no PATO or FLOPO term. The fruit-dehiscence uses should go to review instead of this class.
Negation of the existing FLOPO value accrescent (calyx, receptacle or pedicel not enlarging after flowering).

target: new: colour of a marking (marking quality + colour of the marks)
reason: Two values joined: striped (PATO:0001946 banded, EXACT synonym striped) and green as the colour of the stripes. Neither value alone says that the stripes are green.
Rubbery stems, latex and resin recover their shape after deformation, which is PATO:0001171 elastic. 'Rubbery-succulent' is a compound and is handled by the continuum rule.
The approximate-value pattern with the qualifier 'nearly' applied to the existing FLOPO value equal.
Aristate is already the rule 'awn present' (C207). Its negation says the awn is absent, as for awnless (C347).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum between two values: elliptic PATO_0000947, ovate PATO_0001891)
reason: A compound of two shapes. PATO lists ellipsoid as a synonym of elliptic and ovoid as a synonym of ovate.
A sclerotic margin, scale or calyculus is hardened by thick-walled cells, the same reading as indurate (C305). 'Sclerotic granules' in seeds and fruits are a part (stone cells), not this quality.

target: new: colour of a marking (tinge: secondary colour over the base colour, violet PATO_0001424)
reason: A tinge is a faint second colour over the part's main colour. Mapping it to plain violet would overstate it, and it belongs with the coloured-marking pattern.
Ampulliform means shaped like a flask or ampulla (French 'en forme d'ampoule'): swollen below and narrowed into a neck. That is the definition of FLOPO flask-shaped.
This is not a quality word: the measurement is the length (PATO:0000122) of the awn of the lemma, glume, bract or leaf. The awn is the bearer.
Flocculent means covered with soft woolly tufts. PATO:0104366 floccose lists flocculose and cottony as synonyms.
Cap-shaped stigmas, arils and style bases are dome-like structures sitting over the apex of another part. PATO:0001789 domed is the nearest existing shape, so no new term is needed.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (compound of two values: elongated PATO_0001154, elliptic PATO_0000947)
reason: A compound of two values meaning a narrowly ellipsoid solid, so it needs no single term.
This is a verb fragment ('tending to twine / flake / redden'). The quality is in the following verb, and 'tending' only adds an uncertain tendency.
Same as rule C341 parallel-veined: nerved = veined. Counted forms such as 'parallel-5-nerved' also go to the count-of-parts pattern.
Strongly developed nerves, borders, setae and alar cells are clearly visible and well formed. Conspicuous is the closest reading, but the phrase is a vague degree word.
Tuber-like roots, rhizomes and stems are thickened and swollen like a tuber, which is the definition of FLOPO tuberous.

Bicoloured corollas, seeds and lobules are of two colours, a kind of PATO:0001533 multi-colored. FLOPO discolorous (two leaf surfaces of different colours) is narrower and does not fit seeds or corollas.
'Semi-' weakens the existing value succulent, just as 'sub-' does in the approximate-value pattern. A separate term is not justified.
PATO:0040006 crown like is defined as having a shape like a crown, which covers crown-shaped pappus, discs and gynostemia (French 'en couronne').
